Regulators just entered the AI race. Executives need to pay attention.

This week, two massive moves happened almost simultaneously. The European Commission laid out Digital Markets Act requirements forcing Google to open its AI platform to competitors. And the US Federal Reserve created its own AI task force, led by Marc Andreessen, acknowledging that AI is reshaping the economy faster than they can measure.

The signal is unmistakable: the era of building AI strategy inside a single platform's walled garden is ending. Interoperability mandates mean the platforms you depend on today may be forced to open up to competitors tomorrow. If your product or operations are tightly coupled to one ecosystem's AI capabilities, the regulatory ground is shifting.

Meanwhile, central banks on both sides of the Atlantic are grappling with an economy that does not behave like their models predict — strong productivity, declining white-collar hiring, and massive capital investment in AI infrastructure.

The executives who build platform-agnostic AI architectures now will have strategic optionality. The ones who wait will re-architect under pressure.
